nodes.description: NIK is required in non-haematopoietic lymph-node stromal cells for lymph-node and Peyer's patch organogenesis, through the lymphotoxin-beta receptor. nodes.description: NIK is required in medullary thymic epithelial cells for their maturation and for the establishment of central tolerance. Its loss impairs negative thymic selection, so autoreactive T cells escape; because the defect is in non-haematopoietic thymic stroma, haematopoietic stem cell transplantation does not repair it.

nodes.description: Without NIK activity, IKK-alpha is not phosphorylated, p100 accumulates and is not processed to p52, and unprocessed p100 sequesters RelB. The RelB-p52 transcription factor therefore fails to form and translocate to the nucleus, so the gene programme downstream of BAFFR, CD40 and the lymphotoxin-beta receptor is not activated.

nodes.description: Mice with NIK ablated specifically in thymic epithelial cells fail to develop medullary thymic epithelial cells, break central tolerance, and develop fatal autoimmune destruction, modelling the thymic central-tolerance arm of the human disease.

The alymphoplasia (aly) mouse carries a spontaneous point mutation in the C-terminal interaction domain of Nik and is the classic model of the disease. It lacks all lymph nodes and Peyer's patches, has disorganized splenic and thymic architecture, and is immunodeficient; transgenic wild-type Nik restores these structures.
Homozygous MAP3K14 c.1694C>G, p.Pro565Arg in the index consanguineous pedigree. Pro565 sits near the ATP-coordinating centre of the kinase domain; the substitution renders NIK catalytically inactive.
